repairAudit.claim: Removed the exact duplicate terminal SATISFIED/D-096 reviewGuidance line appended at v15. One copy remains.
repairAudit.result: VERIFIED-REPAIRED on both conditions the v15 findings set
evidence: Both v15 findings are the same defect, which I confirmed by reading them rather than inferring it from the single claimed repair: CLAUDE-V15-S1 locates 'Do not mark DR-101 SATISFIED. Never mint a D-096 (A) grant.' at reviewGuidance indices 32 and 35, and DCIC-V15-S1 reports a Counter over the 36-element array finding that exact value twice. Same string, same indices, same remedy. There is no second, unaddressed finding hiding behind the singular 'claimed repair'.

The removal is exact. In v15 the string occurs at [32] and [35]; in v16 it occurs only at [32]. A Counter over the whole v16 array reports zero exact duplicates of any element, so the fix is complete rather than local. Lines beginning 'Do not mark DR-101 SATISFIED' are now [12], the bare historical single copy, and [32], the combined prohibition - two textually distinct lines, which matches CLAUDE-V15-S1's own fairnessNote that the non-identical v14 variant was not the filed defect.

The edit is surgical: a positional diff shows elements 0 through 34 byte-identical to v15, with only index 35 replaced. The freed terminal slot carries the customary per-generation line, 'Attack any silent v15-to-v16 path outside basedOn.method / honestyRepairsFromV15.' That satisfies CLAUDE-V15-S1's fix note, which allowed closing the append with a refusal line only if it were made textually distinct.

Codex's requiredRepair set two conditions, not one - 'roster reviewGuidance as an edit and remove the newly appended duplicate' - and I checked the second because this list has been governed as append-only. /reviewGuidance is on basedOn.method's closed roster, so the departure from append-only is declared. basedOn.method also names both finding ids, and honestyRepairsFromV15 records the repair as 'DCIC-V15-S1 / CLAUDE-V15-S1', crediting both reviewers rather than one.

This defect family has a bad history in this artifact - DCIC-V6-S1 raised it, v7 falsely claimed to have fixed it, and v8 actually removed it. v16 does not repeat the v7 pattern: the claim in honestyRepairsFromV15 is true of v16's own bytes, which I verified by counting rather than by reading the claim.

advisories.title: notFoldedThisSuccessor now carries eleven declined advisories across four reviewers and many generations, with no recorded rationale for carrying the class indefinitely
advisories.detail: The ledger books CLAUDE-V4-ADV-1..3, Claude v2 ADV-1..ADV-4, Codex v4 DCIC-V4-A1/A2, and CLAUDE-V5-ADV-1..2 as recorded-but-not-folded, plus the historical notes that Codex did not review v1 and that relative notFolded sentences are kept as history rather than rewritten. The booking is honest and each item is traceable to a carried, digest-verified entry, which is exactly the discipline this chain asks for.
advisories.whyNotAFinding: Advisories are not an ACCEPT bar, the artifact discloses rather than drops them, and none bears on the repair under review. Filing this as SHOULD-FIX would deny acceptance over an accumulation the artifact is being transparent about.
advisories.suggestion: A later successor should either fold them or record once why the class is carried indefinitely, so 'not folded this successor' stops being the standing answer by default. I have raised the same pattern in the sibling SARIF and anti-lockstep chains; noting it here for consistency, not as a bar.

whatIsSoundInV16: The repair is minimal and complete at once: one element replaced, a 35-element prefix preserved byte-identical, zero exact duplicates left anywhere in the list, and the freed slot used for the standard next-generation attack line rather than left short.

It honours the less visible half of the required repair. Codex asked for the reviewGuidance edit to be rostered, and it is - which is what keeps a deletion from a historically append-only list from being a silent scope change.

The idCollisionNote is the strongest example of id-qualification discipline I have seen in this corpus: it maps each generation's bare local ids to their qualified form, so a reader can resolve any recorded id back to the frozen verdict that issued it.

ACCEPT is that these bytes are internally sound and that the claimed repair holds on both its conditions. It is NOT a statement that DR-101 is discharged: the row stays OPEN, the artifact remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING, DR-101 is ineligible under D-056, and eleven advisories remain owed.
summary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Both v15 reviewers filed the same duplicate-reviewGuidance defect, and v16 repairs it on both of Codex's conditions: the duplicate is removed with one copy remaining at index 32 and zero exact duplicates anywhere in the list, and /reviewGuidance is rostered as an edit so the departure from append-only is declared rather than silent. The edit is surgical - a 35-element prefix preserved byte-identical, with the freed terminal slot carrying the standard next-generation attack line. The delta is 24 leaves, zero unrostered, zero removed, no design path touched. Remeasurement hygiene is exact, with v15 demoted to HISTORICAL and v16 the only LIVE block, all its pins reproducing. All 22 pinned verdict entries are faithful under the artifact's declared id-qualification convention, and referential integrity is clean. One non-blocking advisory records eleven advisories now riding unfolded.
